messages:
Dina: Heads-up — after yesterday's INT8 rollout on canary we saw KV memory creep on long-context jobs and a small but consistent p95 latency bump. Not a catastrophic regression but reproducible on 2 hosts.
Park: Can you paste the perf counters? I ran a quick profile overnight, looks like slot fragmentation increased and eviction churn spiked during long requests. KV hit rate down ~3.7%. p50 unchanged, p95 +7%.
Dina: Logs: slabmap fragmentation up from 6% -> 18% on canary. Eviction rate went from ~200/s -> ~1200/s during a 10k token trace. Observed more partial-slot writes after INT8 quant paths.
Park: Interesting — INT8 codepath changes alignment and packing, which reduces per-slot size but increases small free holes due to prefetching heuristics. Kernel selection also picked a different GEMM kernel for short sequences which may change allocation cadence.
Jamie: Quick hypothesis: INT8 reduces memory per KV page but increases allocation churn because we now hit the singleflight path more often when slots don't perfectly fit. That + batching heuristic (longctx coalescing disabled on canary) -> more frequent small allocations and LRU churn.
Ryan: EvictBot report from hosts rtx-11 and rtx-12 at 03:14:22 UTC: high_eviction_alert, evictions=1187, avg_slot_util=0.42, fragmentation=0.18. (auto-posted)
EvictBot: "action_required: investigate warmup/prefetch; recommend temporary bump eviction_threshold to 0.65 for canary"
Dina: Re-ran the microbench with profiling enabled. Attached snippet of kernel selection trace: 
```
model: open-variant-7b, seq=4096
kernel: matmul_int8_xp_opt_v3 selected at step 42
batching: continuous_batching ON, coalesce_window=8ms
kv: slot_size=8192 bytes, quant=INT8
```
Memory allocator trace shows many small free extents ~512-1024 bytes.
Park: That matches. Prefetch window of 8ms + INT8 smaller pages -> more 'page tail' holes. Two quick mitigations to A/B: 1) enable slab coalescing pass on eviction to compact small holes, 2) increase prefetch coalescing window from 8ms -> 20ms to let allocator amortize writes.
Jamie: Also consider kernel fallback policy: if sequence > 2048, prefer BF16 kernel for canary until we stabilize the allocator. BF16 uses slightly more memory but fewer allocation churns per trace. We can gate by route tag.
Ryan: For telemetry: add a KV signal 'frag_ratio' and expose per-route p95 with quant-mode tag. Also emit a small sample of slot-size-distribution every 5m for canary hosts. That will let us correlate recall/accuracy vs frag.
Dina: On accuracy side — we saw a tiny BLEU/recall drop on eval prompts: mean R@1 dropped 0.9% when INT8 + aggressive eviction. Could be due to stale KV slots being evicted earlier.
Park: We should quantify: run an A/B with identical batching but different eviction_thresholds. Metric matrix: p95 latency, cost/tokens, kv_hit_rate, recall_delta. 1-week run should surface signal.
Jamie: Quick config patch to test on canary (will push after review):
```
kv.eviction_threshold = 0.65
kv.slab_coalesce = true
batch.coalesce_window_ms = 20
kernel.fallback.seq_threshold = 2048
```
Dina: I'll queue the patch to canary 2 hosts and spin up monitoring dashboards. Can someone own the recall A/B? Park?
Park: I can own the recall A/B and automated evaluation harness. Will also add slot-size histogram to telemetry.
Ryan: I'll add the new signals to Console and wire alerts if frag_ratio > 0.15 + kv_hit_rate drop > 2%. Also prepare rollback plan: auto-fallback to BF16 kernel and restore old eviction threshold.
Dina: Great. If we get >1% recall regression we'll roll back kernel selector for that model. Thanks all — will post updates here after 12h run. :thumbsup:
Jamie: Thanks — please paste perf graphs here when ready.
Park: Will do. Early note: prefetch window tweak reduced eviction churn ~30% in synthetic memtest. Promising but need real workload run.
Dina: Update @ 12:23 UTC: canary hosts running patched config. Initial 2h snapshot: fragmentation down to 11%, evictions -40%, p95 back within +2% baseline. Recall delta at 0.2% so far.
Ryan: Nice. Keep the run for 48h and then schedule a canary rollout with staged ramp if stable.
Dina: Ack — leaving patch on canary. Will report final numbers tomorrow.
